5501.t: From βρέχω (brékhō, “to rain”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix).

5530.t: Thematicization of δάμνημι (dámnēmi, “to subdue”). Cognates include Sanskrit दाम्यति (dāmyati), Latin domō.

5541.t: From an earlier unattested *δημιο-ϝεργός (*dēmio-wergós), from a univerbation of δήμια ἔργα (dḗmia érgă).

5576.t: From an earlier verbal adjective *δίπλατος (*dĭ́plătos), from Proto-Indo-European *dwi-*pl̥-to-s (“twofold”); compare English twofold. By surface analysis, δι- (dĭ-) + -πλάσιος (-plắsĭos).

5524.t: Uncertain. Commonly linked to γρυπός (grūpós, “hook-nosed; aquiline”), which is from Proto-Indo-European *ger- (“to turn, twist, bend, wind”), related to Old English crumb, crump (“bent, crooked”), Old High German krump.

5508.t: From Proto-Hellenic *génewyom, from the root of γένυς (génŭs, “jaw, mouth”).

5504.t: According to Beekes, probably of onomatopoeic origin. A connection with Armenian կորկ (kork, “dirt”) remains very doubtful.

5505.t: Unknown, but Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin in view of the suffix -υχος. Often connected with βότρυς (bótrus, “bunch of grapes”).

5506.t: Probably from Egyptian bꜣkt (“oil flask”). Beekes dismisses any relation with Latin fiscus (“basket”) and βαυκάλιον (baukálion, “jug, pitcher”).

5507.t: Unknown; a candidate for Pre-Greek origin.

5510.t: From the root of γίγνομαι (gĭ́gnomai, “to be born”) from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁-.

5574.t: From διοικέω (dĭoikéō, “to manage, administer”) + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).

5527.t: Inherited from Proto-Indo-European *gómos, a derivation of *gem- (“to press together; to grasp”) and so related to γέμω (gémō, “to be full of”), γέντο (génto, “he/she grasped”), Latin gemō (“to sigh, groan”) and Proto-Slavic *žęti (“to press, squeeze”).

5538.t: From δεύτερος (deúteros, “second”) + νόμος (nómos, “law”) + -ιον (-ion). Translates Biblical Hebrew מִשְׁנֵה הַתּוֹרָה (mišnê hattôrâ).
